Tuesday,

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the paradox that in the time of the Purim exile, the Jews fulfilled what they had already accepted at the Giving of the Torah, a matter of "wondrous" transcendence beyond all comparison.

translations.translation: "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do"1,
and it is explained in this by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, our leader, in his well-known maamar2
which he said on Purim Katan
in Moscow
[which this year is the beginning of the Jubilee3
second4
of its recitation]
that now, in the time of exile, they accepted what they had already begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah.
And as the words of our Sages, of blessed memory5,
on the verse6
"They fulfilled and accepted the Jews, etc.",
that they fulfilled now
(in the days of Achashverosh)
what they had already accepted at the time of the Giving of the Torah.
And he precisely notes in this maamar,
that at first glance it is a wondrous thing
[and he precisely notes in his question that this is a matter of "wondrous"
(and not like the usual language in most maamarim – "it needs to be understood")
because the matter
(that they accepted in the time of exile what they had begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah)
is in the aspect of wondrous.
And as explained7
regarding the matter of "It is not wondrous... and not distant"8,
that distance and closeness are relative to each other,
but "wondrous" indicates a matter of separation and distinction, even to the point that it is in the aspect of "wonder" relative to it,
and this means it is a matter that is entirely incomparable.
And as is known9
(regarding the Sefiros)
that the aspect of "wonder" is the aspect of Kesser,
and in particular, the aspect of the innerness of Kesser,
which is entirely beyond comprehension in relation to the entire order of the chain of descent.
And from this it will be understood also regarding the matter of the wondrous mentioned in the maamar],
that at the Giving of the Torah
(when they began to do)
the Jewish people were at the ultimate level of elevation and in a most praiseworthy state and condition,
and it was then after the Splitting of the Sea and the Exodus from Egypt,
which are matters that established each and every Jew and the entirety of the Jewish people in a most elevated state,
for in the Exodus from Egypt, the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself upon them in His glory and redeemed them,
and at the time of the Splitting of the Sea
[which is the conclusion and seal of the Exodus from Egypt10]
a maidservant saw at the sea what the prophets did not see11,
and certainly the ultimate elevation of the Jewish people at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
for the Giving of the Torah was only once, as is known12
that the Giving of the Torah will not occur again,
and it is also explained in Tanya13
that at the time of the Giving of the Torah there was already a semblance of the ultimate perfection of the world that will be in the future,
which was a revelation of G-dliness in tangible sight,
that due to these revelations the Jewish people were at the ultimate level.
In contrast, in the time of exile it is the exact opposite,
that the Jewish people are at the lowest point of descent.
And especially in the time of Haman
(when "And the Jews accepted, etc., they fulfilled, etc." occurred)
who sought, Heaven forbid, to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews, from youth to elder, infants and women, in one day, etc.14,
for this decree was most severe, as it was all at once upon all the Jews throughout the entire world,
for Achashverosh ruled over the entire globe, as stated in the Midrash15,
and it was impossible to escape to a place that was already after the decree, since it was in one day
(throughout the entire world),
which is
(within the exile itself)
the most terrible exile.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the core of Haman's decree was against Jewish education, targeting the young children, which requires mesirus nefesh to protect and establish them in their proper place.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the maamar there that the force of
(the decree and)
the exile in spirituality was the decree regarding the matter of education.
And as stated in the Midrash16
[Haman] said
(Haman)
"I will not send my hand first except upon these children."
And this means that in order to carry out, Heaven forbid, his evil plot and wicked thought which he thought against the Jews, may G-d have mercy, to destroy them17,
the beginning is with these children of the study hall.
For the intention in this is the decree upon the entirety of the matter of education,
and it can be said that even though in the above "young students" refers to a child in years, but analogous to this is also a child in matters of Judaism,
even if he is an adult in years, and in the language of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, "he already has white hair",
nevertheless, in his state regarding matters of Torah and mitzvos he is in the aspect of a child.
[And from this very fact
(that the existence of the Jewish people depends on education)
one understands the greatness of the self-sacrifice that must be for the education of the Jewish people.
For one must give his soul so that "Do not touch My anointed ones"18
refers to these children of the study hall, as stated in Tractate Shabbos19,
which is accomplished by bringing the children to their proper place,
to the study hall,
and there itself, the manner of education is in a manner of "house
(of study)
" and permanent,
meaning that the children will receive from their teacher the foundation
(the entire structure)
for all the days of their lives].
